summary: Universität Hamburg, one of Germany's largest universities, charges no tuition to international degree students. The only regular cost is the semester contribution, which rose to €402 for winter 2026/27 and includes a public-transport ticket.
covers: No tuition fees for international students on degree programmes.
A semester contribution of €402 for winter 2026/27, which includes the Studierendenwerk contribution and the semester transport ticket.
No living allowance from the university; for a visa, plan to prove €11,904 for your first year.
eligibility: Open to all nationalities with qualifications recognised for the level you apply to.
Most bachelor's programmes are taught in German. Master's programmes vary — several are in English, each with its own language requirements.
Master's applicants must meet the programme's subject requirements, which are checked against your transcript.
how_to_apply: Pick a programme and read its entry requirements and language rules.
Apply online through the university's application platform (STiNE). Upload documents only when asked; posted paper documents are discarded.
Winter-semester windows for 2026/27 were: master's 1 May – 15 June; bachelor's 1 June – 15 July. For a summer-semester bachelor's start, the window is 1 December – 15 January.
Check your programme page: some master's programmes set earlier deadlines for non-EU applicants (31 December in some cases).
watch_out: Master's deadlines (mid-June) come a month before bachelor's deadlines — don't assume one date fits all.
Individual programmes can override the general dates. The programme page always wins.
Hamburg housing is expensive and competitive; start looking as soon as you apply.

sources.title: Universität Hamburg — Checklist for international master's enrolment, winter 2026/27 (PDF)
German Federal Foreign Office — Visa fees

costs: Semester contribution (€402 for winter 2026/27, including a public-transport pass for greater Hamburg)
Health insurance — about €145 a month with a public insurer; students from outside the EU who are over 30 on arrival generally need private cover
Living costs — about €1,000–€1,600 a month; a student-hall room is usually €350–€450
You. For the visa you must first prove €11,904 for your first year
documents: Your online application in STiNE, with only the documents your programme asks for — paper documents sent by post are not considered
Proof of the language of instruction your programme requires (German for most bachelor's degrees)
After admission: online enrolment within 7 days of your admission letter — this deadline is final
Your first degree certificate for a master's; if it is not issued yet, submit it by the end of your first semester (31 March or 30 September)
Your health-insurance status (insured or exempt), reported to the university by a public health insurer — you cannot be enrolled without it

faq.q: How quickly must I enrol after I am admitted?
faq.a: Within 7 days of receiving your admission letter. Hamburg says this deadline is final and cannot be extended, so have your documents ready before the letter arrives.

faq.q: Do I need German health insurance?
faq.a: Yes. To enrol you must be insured with a public health insurer, or exempted through one, and the insurer reports your status to the university electronically.

faq.q: Is studying in Hamburg really free?
faq.a: Tuition is free, but you pay the semester contribution (€402 for winter 2026/27, which includes a transport pass), health insurance and living costs of roughly €1,000–€1,600 a month.
